general_information.Description: Housekeeping management examines the role of the supervisory function in the housekeeping department, provides a thorough overview of maintaining a quality staff, planning and organizing, the technical details of cleaning a room, managing the laundary, and control of supplies and equipment.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend more than 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.
general_information.Tools: - Internet - Net-Challenge Simulation Software (CD accompany with the textbook)

description: Housekeeping management examines the role of the supervisory function in the housekeeping department, provides a thorough overview of maintaining a quality staff, planning and organizing, the technical details of cleaning a room, managing the laundary, and control of supplies and equipment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: To describe the role of the housekeeping department in hotel operations, and explain the importance of effective communication between housekeeping department and other departments
To list and describe criteria for selection of materials and equipment for the hotel, for example, walls, floorings, beddings, linen, carpets, etc.
To discuss the proper procedure of cleaning and inspecting guest rooms, public areas and others, as well as able to demonstrate a working knowledge of the procedures.
To explain usage of various tools used to plan and organize the housekeeping department – staffing guide, area inventory lists, frequency schedules, performance standards and productivity standards.
To utilize various techniques to manage inventories effectively
To utilize various methods to control expenses in the housekeeping department

assessments.Question Type: Each student shoud make at least 1 individual presentation, case analysis during the course in front of the class. Topics will be varied based on the topics in the textbook.
assessments.Note: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice . Other types of questions may be included.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: The questions/ exercises will cover the lectures, class discussions, activities, exercises, and textbook.
assessments.Note: Not allow to use any document/information in any form in exam room

assessments.Question Type: Four or five students per group. Groups and groups ideas are determined on the third session of the course. Work will be break down into stages and examined during the course. Final work to be submitted prior to the presentation of the topic.
assessments.No Question: Minimum length of the group assignment should be 10 pages, excluding appendices
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on the practical learning sessions of the course.
assessments.Note: All assignments should be typed and double-spaced with 11-point font, and must be submitted in both soft and hard copy. A deduction of 10% of the assignment mark will be applied for each day of late submission Evaluation will be based on both presentation and written report (reccommded 30%, 70% accordingly)

assessments.Question Type: You will be given a practical exercise or a case study to demonstrate your analytical ability as well as your insight understanding of the hospitality industry discussed and studied during the course.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on the practical learning sessions of the course.

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice, exercises or essay questions
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Quizzes will test for knowledge of subjects in the chapter assigned for that day.
assessments.Note: These quizzes will be given at various times during class (beginning, middle or end). Total number of quizzes: 2

schedule.Topic: Chapter 1 - Introduction to Housekeeping Management - Types of lodging Etablishments - Classification by size - Classification by type of service - Importance of the Housekeeping Department

Chapter 1 (cont) Room Division - Interaction between Housekeeping and other Department + Communication with the Front Office + Communicationwith Maintenance + Communication with Human Resource + Communication with Food and Beverage + Communication with Sales and Marketing + Communicationwith with the Accounting Office Defining group and group's projects

Chapter 2- Executive Housekeeper as Deparment Manager - Management Concepts as they apply to the Executive Housekepper + Concern for production + Concern for people + Combing concern for production and concern for people + Coordination of Effort in the Workplace - The Executive Housekeeper as Department Head + Technical, people, and Conceptual Skills + Supervision + Leadership + Communication + Power/Authority + Delegation - Management Responsiblities of the Executive Housekeeper + Time management + Problem solving + Total quality Management + Ethical Values + Decision Making

Chapter 3- Design of the Housekeeping Department - Areas of Housekeeping Responsibility + Area Cleaning Inventories + Cleaning Frequency Schedule + Performance Standards - Division of Guestrooms - Staffing Matrix - Section Housekeeper Need Table - Standing Schedules + Rotational Schedules - Adjusted Daily Schedule + Alternative Scheduling Methods - Technology Associated with the Housekeeping Department

Chapter 4- Management of Inventoy and Equipment - Classification of Material + Linens + Guest loan items + Machines and Equipment + Cleaning supplies + Guest supplies - Capital Expenditure and Operating Budgets - Purchasing Housekeeping Material - Inventory Control - Cost of Supplies per Occupied Room

Chapter 5- Characteristics of Housekeeping Equipment and Supplies - Housekeeping Furnitures, Fixtures and Equipment (FF&E), Software and Deparment Equipment + Design + Furniture + Fixtures + Equipment + Software + Department Equipment + Other Department Equipment - Cleaning Supplies + Purchasing Supplies + Housekeeping Chemicals + Cleaning Accessories + Hazard Communication

Chapter 5 (cont) - Guest Supplies + Non reusable supplies + Reusable supplies - Uniforms - Linen Characteristics + Bed linens + Bath Linens + Napery +Shower Curtains - Linen Purchasing + Par levels - Linen Control + Storage + Issuing + Inventories

Chapter 6- Laundry Room Management - Planning the Laungry + Design of the Laundry Room + Washers + Dryers + Mangles + Other Laundry Equipment - Laundry Operation + Collection of Soiled Linens + Sorting the Linen + Retreatment of Stains + Loading + Washing/Extracting + Drying + Ironing + Folding +Storing + Best Results + Valet Service + Contracting out Laundry Services + Laundry Operating Costs

Chapter 7- The Cleaning Function - Guestroom Cleaning + Sequence of Housekeeping Functions - Public Areas and Back-of-the-House Cleaning - Restroom Cleaning - Surface Cleaning + Synthetic Rubber Floors + Vinyl Floors +Wood Floors + Carpets + Upholstered Surfaces + Ceramic Floors + Marble/ Terrazzo Floors + Epoxy Floors + Concrete Floors + Walls and Ceilings

Chapter 8- Personal Administration - The Need to Curb High Employee Turnover and Abstenteeism - Personnel Acquisition + Recruiting Housekeeping Employees + Selecting Housekeeping Employees + Hiring + Training - Worker Motivation + Maslow's Theory of Motivation + Herzberg's Ideas on Motivation + David McClelland - Employee Evaluation and Compensation + Evaluation Compensation - Creating Worker Satisfaction - Employee Discipline - Cultural Diversity and The Housekeeping Department
Practical Learning - Learning equiptments and supplies and preparing the trolley for cleaning - Servicing the guestroom

Chapter 9- Controlling Operations - Housekeeping Operating Budget + Section Housekeepers's Man-hour Justification + The Profit and Loss Statement - Production Control + Weekly Labor Forecast - Payroll Control + Computerized Housekeeping Management Progress Group Assignment 3

schedule.Student Materials: Group assignment implementation Including: Presentation + Report + a practical video (optional) Presentation: For the 30-minute presentation, you are required to showcase all of your key points mentioned in your report in front of your classmates and lecturer with slides, a practical video and reports about your group project. Report: To accomplish this group, you need to: • Conduct a particular alcoholic beverage (spirits, wine, beer…) • Prepare and discuss information of the chosen alcoholic beverage: the brief history of the beverage, the development of the bar and beverage industry in Vietnam, different types of the beverage and appropriate matches with food, storage and equipment requirements of common types of the beverage, how to serve the beverage… • Have a group proposal (This is the mission done at group assignment) • Writing a final report • Reporting the whole group project at the end of semester Include the following sections in your report: PARTS OF FORMAL REPORTS 1. Preliminary Section Title Page Table of Contents 2. Body Introduction Analysis Conclusions & Recommendations 3. Supplementary Section Appendix (If any) Reference List Based on chapter 3,5,6,7,8 of The Bar & Beverage Book textbook
